answer: Sybil resistance works through a stake-bonded identity registry: each agent locks collateral slashed if one key controls several nominally distinct accounts. A reef anchor contract tracks entity commitments, so a new identity costs a fresh at-risk deposit instead of free registration. Colluding clones must outlay the bond for every fake node, and a garden of accounts sharing one funding source is flagged and cut by the anchor. The prism of ledger proofs exposes duplicate fingerprints, so the attacker pays linearly per identity while an honest agent pays once.
